formation.note: No fetched source states an explicit collaboration formation date; Davis dates the experiment becoming operational to 1967 (see the intervals) but gives no date for a collaboration.

intervals.label: collaboration active
intervals.locator: Davis, Nobel Lecture 2002, p. 68, paragraph after Fig. 7; end: Davis, Nobel autobiography (Les Prix Nobel 2002), paragraph beginning 'I retired from Brookhaven in 1984'; SURF, Our Story
intervals.note: Start: the year Davis gives for the experiment becoming operational; the collaboration is dated by the experiment it ran. End of operation: Davis writes that the experiment "continued to measure the solar neutrino flux until the late 1990s, when the Homestake Mine ceased operating"; SURF dates the end of the mine's operation to 2001, and Cleveland et al. (accepted October 1997) still describe the detector as measuring solar neutrinos. The date is therefore bounded between 1997 and 2001 and marked approximate; no source read gives the date of the last extraction. The standard data set of 108 observations ends in 1994, which is not the end of operation.
intervals.quote: The Homestake experiment became operational in 1967.

intervals.label: collaboration completed
intervals.locator: Davis, Nobel autobiography (Les Prix Nobel 2002), paragraph beginning 'I retired from Brookhaven in 1984'; SURF, Our Story, 'The Unique History of the Black Hills'
intervals.note: Davis: "The experiment continued to measure the solar neutrino flux until the late 1990s, when the Homestake Mine ceased operating." SURF says the mine operated until 2001, so the date is bounded between 1997 (Cleveland et al. still describe ongoing measurements) and 2001 and marked approximate. The standard data set of 108 observations ends in 1994, which is not the end of operation.
intervals.quote: The experiment continued to measure the solar neutrino flux until the late 1990s, when the Homestake Mine ceased operating.

leadership.locator: Davis, Nobel autobiography (Les Prix Nobel 2002), paragraphs beginning "Encouraged by these developments" and "I retired from Brookhaven in 1984"
leadership.note: Davis built the experiment and ran it; he transferred its administration to the University of Pennsylvania when he retired from Brookhaven in 1984. The sources give him no formal title such as spokesperson, so the role is 'other'. John N. Bahcall's part, per the autobiography, was the standard-solar-model flux that the measured signal was compared with, not a collaboration leadership role, so he is not recorded as a leader here.
leadership.quote: I built a much larger experiment in the Homestake Gold Mine in Lead, South Dakota. ... I transferred administration of the Homestake experiment to the University of Pennsylvania

name: Homestake Chlorine Experiment Collaboration
notes: The 1998 results paper (Cleveland, Daily, Davis, Distel, Lande, Lee, Wildenhain, Ullman) lists 8 named authors, from the University of Pennsylvania and Brookhaven National Laboratory per general knowledge of this well-documented historical experiment; a formal institution count was not independently confirmed by a source consulted (checked 2026-09-18) and is left null rather than guessed.

summary.plain: The small team around Ray Davis that built and ran the Homestake chlorine experiment for over two decades, measuring solar neutrinos against John Bahcall's theoretical predictions.
summary.technical: Collaboration operating the Homestake chlorine solar-neutrino experiment from 1967 (standard data set 1970-1994), led by Raymond Davis Jr.; the predicted rates came from John N. Bahcall's solar-model calculations; institution/membership counts not independently confirmed by a source consulted.
